userPrompts.text: I had an idea to have the resume chat give you the option to choose to resume in copilot, codex or claude code. Should I put that in the Pro version?
currently the resume only resumes into copilot. Create a plan to have resume go back to the same agent it came from.
Continue from where you left off.
when I start the pro version do I keep the free part open source license the same?

firstResponse: Let me look at how the project is structured so I can give you a grounded answer rather than a generic one.
lastResponse: Good question to settle now, before any Pro code exists. First, a fact about your current setup: [package.json](package.json#L8) declares `"license": "MIT"`, but there's **no `LICENSE` file at the repo root** (the only LICENSE files are in `node_modules`). Worth adding the actual MIT text — right now the license is asserted but not shipped. (Not legal advice — but here's the practical shape of the decision.) ## Short answer Yes, you can keep the free part MIT and add a paid Pro tier — that's the standard **open-core** model. But *how* you structure it matters, because MIT is very permissive. ## What MIT does and doesn't let you do - **You can keep selling Pro alongside an MIT free core.** Nothing about MIT forces Pro to be open. Pro just has to live in code you *don't* publish under MIT. - **MIT is irrevocable per release.** Any version you've already shipped as MIT stays MIT forever. Y…
